runs.text: PYGAME FINAL PROJECT
TANK
SHOOTERS
One arena. Two tanks. One winner.
1v1 2D shooting game
Developed by Ilyas Akinola
Game artwork: Kenney Top-down Tanks pack, supplied in the project assets folder. Content: Ilyas Akinola’s project brief and finalproject.py.
Tank Shooters is a local two-player game. The tagline highlights the single-arena duel.
Game concept & goals
A strategic tank duel where quick decisions
and smart positioning decide the winner.
PLAYER OBJECTIVE
Reduce your opponent’s health to zero
while keeping your own tank alive. Use
cover and power-ups to gain an advantage.
TARGET EXPERIENCE
Exciting competition with a friend, followed
by the satisfaction of a hard-fought victory.
Game artwork: Kenney Top-down Tanks pack, supplied in the project assets folder. Content: Ilyas Akinola’s project brief and finalproject.py.
Both players share one keyboard. Each tank begins with three health points in the current code. Pickups are optional advantages rather than a separate win condition.
Gameplay & key features
PLAY ON ONE KEYBOARD
P1: WASD to move, Space to shoot
P2: Arrows to move, Enter to shoot
Trees and obstacles create cover
and block movement and shots.
Random pickups grant a shield,
double speed or rapid fire.
Built for shared play and friendly rivalry.
PYTHON TOOLS IN THE GAME
pygame
Library for sprites, input and rendering.
random
Module for pickup positions and types.
now
Variable storing elapsed time in seconds.
Rect.colliderect()
Pygame method for rectangle collisions.
Game artwork: Kenney Top-down Tanks pack, supplied in the project assets folder. Content: Ilyas Akinola’s project brief and finalproject.py.

Terminology: random is a Python standard-library module. pygame is a library. now is a variable calculated as pygame.time.get_ticks() / 1000, giving elapsed time since Pygame initialization, not a clock time or a library. Rect.colliderect() tests rectangle overlap, not the exact painted outlines of sprites. POWERUP_DURATION is five seconds; a shield is consumed when it blocks a hit.
GAMEPLAY
DEMO
Switch to the running Pygame app for the live demonstration. Show movement and shooting, obstacle collisions, a pickup, and the end of a round. Return to the presentation afterward.
Development & challenges
Over two weeks, I completed the core game logic,
including 1v1 shooting, theme music and visuals.
Random pickup placement
Challenge: keep random spawns inside
the map and away from obstacles.
I revisited the random module, limited the
spawn coordinates and checked for nearby
obstacles and tanks before placing a pickup.
Keeping the barrel aligned
Challenge: make the barrel turn with
the tank and stay attached.
I made the barrel follow the tank’s angle
and update its position from the tank’s
center each frame.
Game artwork: Kenney Top-down Tanks pack, supplied in the project assets folder. Content: Ilyas Akinola’s project brief and finalproject.py.

The development duration is the developer’s own account. In _try_spawn_pickup(), randint chooses coordinates within the arena and colliderect rejects crowded positions. Barrel.update() uses the tank angle and calculates an offset from its center. The project includes theme.mp3 and calls pygame.mixer.music.play(-1) to repeat the track.
